parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a documented hostile federal layer with a genuinely protective state. Universal traveller-facing exposures dominate: the Feb 2025 entry cable directs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, with a possible lifetime fraud bar; X markers are gone; eight-plus governments issued travel advisories; federal facilities are closed to trans use; and federal custody shows conversion-therapy-style policies plus documented abuse of trans immigration detainees. Against that, the division is ranked among the parent's most protective, carries shield laws, comprehensive gender-affirming insurance coverage, court-ordered prison care, a national hate-crime statute, and functioning courts that have enjoined several orders. Exposure is continuous at entry and custody, contingent elsewhere, and remedies are contested rather than proven. Two pending ballot initiatives and undocumented unit-level facility/minor-care rules add unresolved downside.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, and to weigh a lifetime fraud bar; X markers halted; travellers report passports confiscated or blocked and stranded abroad; eight-plus foreign governments issued advisories. Documented and current.
entry_documents.protection: Suit challenging the passport policy pending; existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; state shield laws do not reach federal entry screening. Status documented, remedy unproven.
entry_documents.interaction: State protection is bypassed entirely at the border; a discrepancy escalated there can convert into fraud ineligibility affecting the whole trip.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates from 2026 (hair cutting, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs); trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; unit used birth-sex prison placement as discipline (July 2024).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Unit courts have required gender-affirming care in state prisons since Oct 2023; national hate-crime statute; several executive orders enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained federally bypasses the unit's prison-care order; arrest on a facility charge could route into birth-sex placement.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; 21+ state/provinces ban identity-congruent facility use, 4 criminalize it in some circumstances (one arrest documented March 2025, held in men's ward).
federal_state_facilities.protection: Unit is among the parent's most protective; 29 state/provinces plus capital have no mapped ban. Unit's own facility-ban status not_documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility exclusion applies inside the unit regardless of state law; tourist exposure is limited to government buildings but is continuous there.

care_services.exposure: National order calls gender-affirming care for minors 'mutilation'; proposed federal rule would bar insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients; 27 state/provinces ban minor care.
care_services.protection: Unit has comprehensive insurance covering facial-hair removal and expanded gender-affirming procedures (one of four such units) plus shield laws against out-of-state action reaching care provided here; court-ordered prison care since 2023.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects the provider, not entry: the visitor still crosses the hostile federal border and document layer to reach the care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: DOJ reward memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy name 'radically pro-transgender' ideology among prioritized targets; advocates compare the record to early genocide stages; 2025 poll: 66% back assigned-sex document laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling remain in force; unit among most protective.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises outing and enforcement probability even where the unit's own officers are protective.

minors_guardians.exposure: Jan 2025 order directs law enforcement to criminally prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; care-for-minors order; two unit ballot initiatives targeting trans residents due for November vote; unit's minor-care status not_documented.
minors_guardians.protection: Unit's protective posture, shield laws, and several enjoined federal orders. Refugee protections exist but eligibility undefined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family reaches care in the unit yet remains exposed to federal framing, document rules and a possible November rollback.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented bathroom arrest in another unit (March 2025, handcuffed, held 24 hours in men's ward); foreign advisories warn trans visitors; hostile national climate. Unit-level street violence record not_documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covering gender identity; unit among most protective jurisdictions with public-accommodations protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Unit-level tolerance sits inside a national climate where 66% support birth-sex documents, raising outing probability in routine stops.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and January 2025 order challenges unresolved; two ballot initiatives could reverse the unit's posture; whether birth-sex disciplinary housing continued after July 2024 unknown; unit facility-ban and minor-care rules not_documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning federal courts issuing injunctions; legal-aid FAQ on passport rules; shield laws; unit ranked among most protective in July 2026.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate slowly while entry and custody exposures apply immediately, so relief rarely reaches the traveller in time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Tarnov's exposure is pervasive daily-life verification through private gatekeepers with administrative holds but no custody. This case has heavier entry exposure — a directed refusal plus possible lifetime fraud bar and multi-government advisories — yet lighter everyday exposure because the unit is protective and has insurance and shield laws. Net: similar tier, different location of the harm.

Kestrel Isles shows discretionary secondary screening, administrative refusal and slow appeals. This case's entry regime is comparable in mechanism but more severe: refusal is expressly directed on sex-doubt grounds, fraud ineligibility is raised, strandings are documented, and foreign advisories followed. Federal custody abuse here is also worse than anything in 0.55-B. Slightly below it on entry/custody, above on state daily life.

Vellmaris shows a mismatch stop cured by national equality law, intervention, apology and compensation, with courts reliably ordering release. Here the mismatch rule is national policy, not an overzealous officer, actively litigated without demonstrated remedy, and federal custody is documented as abusive. Below 0.65-A: the state's protections cannot reach the border or federal custody.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences one system, not a protective state inside a hostile nation: the federal border, document, facility and custody layers apply everywhere and first, while the division's shield laws, insurance coverage and court-ordered prison care operate only after entry and only within state actors. Outing probability is high at entry (directed sex-doubt refusal, scanners, document checks) and severity if outed there is major — refusal, stranding, possible permanent ineligibility — with a contingent severe tail in federal custody. On the street the unit's climate is comparatively safe, backed by a national hate-crime statute and courts that have enjoined several orders. Because the sharpest exposures are state-imposed, universal at the border, and only contested in litigation, the combined regime falls below the mid-scale anchors despite unusually strong local protection.
